input.description: Cyrus readiness audit: flags, coverage, research
input.prompt:
You are doing a READ-ONLY readiness audit of Cyrus (AI game-mod studio inside the Nxeon app) and writing ONE report. Do not edit code, repos, settings, env or production; do not run paid model builds or any build service call; no deploys. Write only the report file `/root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/BM-readiness-audit-2026-10-13.md` (no secrets in it). Use the worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-rc3` (branch release/cyrus-rc3, head 5ada5624f9) to read code; heavy commands only via /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost (rarely needed). Read first: /root/CLAUDE.md, /root/claudeskills/agent-notes/cyrus-research/CYRUS-TRACKER.md (sections 1,3,5,6,7,10 and the last 15), CYRUS-FULL-PLAN.md, GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md, G-gaps.md, docs/cyrus/12-gaps-and-roadmap.md, docs/cyrus/reference/flags-and-env.md, lib/cyrus/admin/flags.ts + readiness.ts, lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json.

The owner's goals: make ANY Minecraft mod from one prompt (simple to massive mechanical mods, textures, sfx, music, models, worldgen), cut token cost, have Cyrus be self-learning/self-improving, later support all games. They want every capability that is switched off or limited to be made ready and turned on where ready.

PART A, flags and limits audit: list EVERY Cyrus switch that is off or unset in production or capability-limited (env CYRUS_*/MB_* and Settings cyrus_*; prod values you may read with `bash /opt/nxeon/scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh flags` and the read-only admin settings catalog; never print secrets). For each: what it enables, current state, evidence it works (tests, real flights in cyrus-research/*-flights-*.json), blockers, risk (customers/money), and a verdict: READY-TURN-ON / NEEDS-WORK(what) / OWNER-DECISION(what) / NEVER-YET. Include specifically: the version selector (registry.json statuses: why 26.x is "preview" and exactly what evidence is needed to promote each version, what exists already), worldgen/datapack studio, creatures, armor and note-block lanes, technique flags, handgun grip fix, test-flight gate options, perf switches, customer app, API v1, library contribution, MB_DEDUPE, effort/model routing knobs, learning loop. End with a short ordered "turn on now" list with the exact variable/setting and expected effect.
PART B, Minecraft one-prompt coverage matrix: for each mod class (items/weapons/armor, mobs/bosses/creatures with models, blocks incl. custom blocks, commands, menus/GUIs/shops, quests/NPCs, HUD, economy, chat/admin tools, minigames, worldgen: biomes/structures/dimensions/ores, enchantments, recipes, advancements, resource packs: textures/models/sounds/music/fonts, datapacks, client-side mods (Fabric/NeoForge), mod packs/import) state: supported today? how (lane), verified how (unit/real flight/real client), known failure modes, what is missing to be reliable from ONE prompt. Rank the top 10 gaps by user impact.
PART C, knowledge and training: inventory what research/knowledge exists (BA reference mods, BD mod-tools survey, BF technique catalogue, universal-modder field notes at /tank/cyrus-knowledge, Modrinth reference corpus at /tank/cyrus-library-staging/_reference-mods: counts, licences, what is private-only) and what has already been distilled into build knowledge (sheets, failure rules, recipes, goldens, prompts) versus NOT yet. Propose a concrete distillation pipeline (mining reference mods into verified recipes/techniques/rules/golden tests, never copying GPL/ARR code, never serving corpus), with estimated paid-model cost per stage (Sonnet-first), and how recipe memory / starter bank (BL-recipe-memory-design.md, BL-token-savings-plan.md) fit. Note: the learning loop must stay review-gated.
PART D, multi-game and self-improvement: gap analysis for onboarding game #2 (docs/cyrus/onboarding/PLAYBOOK.md, games/*, research for hytale/fivem/valheim/terraria/zomboid etc.) and for a truly self-improving engine (outcome telemetry -> mined rules -> eval -> gated release): what exists, what is missing, ordered roadmap, effort and model (Sonnet vs Opus) per step.

Format: tables, terse, every claim labelled V (verified in code/test/flight) or U (estimate). Keep under ~600 lines. Final reply to me: under 200 words with the 5 most important findings and the "turn on now" list size.

## Token economy estimate (config defaults: 500 tokens per $1 of AI cost)
| Plan | Price | Tokens | AI cost if fully spent | Margin before Stripe | Margin after Stripe fee | Typical builds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy the Cyrus build service (services/modbuilder) to the build VM 88001 and rebuild its image. OWNER RUNS THIS
# (on the primary). Agents never run it. Runbook: docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md step 3.
#
# The file list is DERIVED FROM THE DOCKERFILE (every COPY source), so a new module can never be forgotten here
# (test/modbuilder-dockerfile.test.ts checks `--list` against the Dockerfile). The two optional data files come from lib/.
#
#   bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh --list                 print what would be copied, touch nothing
#   bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh                         copy, build TAG, restart, health + guard smoke
#   JDK25=yes bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh               also install JDK 25 + Gradle 9 + the 26.x classpaths
#   API_KEY=sk-ant-... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh      switch the CLI from the subscription login to an API key
#   FLIP=yes ...                                                    open the studio (launch pair) after the smoke, ONLY if /health auth=api_key
# Env: S (service dir, default: this repo), LIBDIR (lib/cyrus of the same tree), TAG (new image, default modbuilder:0.6),
#      MC26_PINS (with JDK25=yes), V/JUMP (VM + jump host).
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
S=${S:-$HERE/../../services/modbuilder}
LIBDIR=${LIBDIR:-$HERE/../../lib/cyrus}
TAG=${TAG:-modbuilder:0.6}
API_KEY="${API_KEY:-}"
FLIP="${FLIP:-no}"
JDK25="${JDK25:-no}"
MC26_PINS="${MC26_PINS:-26.2=26.2.build.133-stable 26.1.2=26.1.2.build.74-stable}"
V=${V:-root@10.20.1.253}
JUMP=${JUMP:-root@178.63.94.114}
SSH="ssh -o BatchMode=yes -J $JUMP"

# Every COPY source of the Dockerfile (optional globs like registry.jso[n] are skipped: they come from LIBDIR below).
files_from_dockerfile() {
  awk '/^COPY /{ n=0; for (i=2;i<NF;i++) { if ($i ~ /^--/) continue; print $i } }' "$S/Dockerfile" | grep -v '\[' | sort -u
}
FILES=$(files_from_dockerfile)
EXTRA="run.sh Dockerfile"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--list" ]; then
  for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do echo "$f"; done
  echo "lib:versions/registry.json"; echo "lib:import/deps.json"
  exit 0
fi
cd "$S" || { echo "no service dir $S"; exit 1; }
missing=""; for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do [ -e "$f" ] || missing="$missing $f"; done
# toolchain.tgz is not in git: it must already sit in /opt/modbuilder on the VM (pinned Temurin 21 + Gradle 8).
missing=$(echo "$missing" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^toolchain.tgz$' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "${missing// /}" ] || { echo "missing in $S:$missing"; exit 1; }
EXPECT_PROMPT=$(sed -n 's/^const PROMPT_VERSION = "\(mb-[0-9.-]*\)";.*/\1/p' prompts.js)
[ -n "$EXPECT_PROMPT" ] || { echo "cannot read PROMPT_VERSION from prompts.js"; exit 1; }

echo "== 1/7 service must be idle"
H=$($SSH $V 'curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health') || { echo "cannot reach the VM"; exit 1; }
echo "$H" | cut -c1-160
echo "$H" | grep -q '"running":0' || { echo "A build is running. Run this again in a minute."; exit 1; }
PREV=$($SSH $V "docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' modbuilder" 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$PREV" ] || { echo "cannot read the running image"; exit 1; }
echo "running image: $PREV  -> new: $TAG  (expect promptVersion $EXPECT_PROMPT)"
$SSH $V "test -f /opt/modbuilder/toolchain.tgz" || { echo "/opt/modbuilder/toolchain.tgz is missing on the VM"; exit 1; }

echo "== 2/7 backup (app files + env) and copy"
TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
BK=/opt/modbuilder/.backup-$TS.tgz
$SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && tar czf $BK --exclude=toolchain.tgz --exclude='.backup-*' . /root/claudebox.env 2>/dev/null; test -s $BK" || { echo "backup failed"; exit 1; }
echo "backup: $BK (restore: tar xzf $BK -C /opt/modbuilder; cp the claudebox.env inside back to /root)"
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
tar -C "$S" -cf - $(for f in $FILES $EXTRA; do [ -e "$f" ] && echo "$f"; done) | $SSH $V 'tar -C /opt/modbuilder -xf -' || exit 1
scp -o BatchMode=yes -o ProxyJump=$JUMP "$LIBDIR/versions/registry.json" "$LIBDIR/import/deps.json" $V:/opt/modbuilder/ || exit 1

if [ -n "$API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "== 3/7 switching auth to the API key (old env kept as claudebox.env.bak-subscription; the login dir is moved aside)"
  $SSH $V "cp -a /root/claudebox.env /root/claudebox.env.bak-subscription && sed -i '/^CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=/d;/^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=/d' /root/claudebox.env && echo 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=$API_KEY' >> /root/claudebox.env && if [ -f /root/.claude-modbuilder/.credentials.json ]; then mv /root/.claude-mod
else
  echo "== 3/7 auth unchanged (the current login stays)"
fi

echo "== 4/7 build $TAG and restart (a few minutes; JDK25=$JDK25)"
ARGS=""
if [ "$JDK25" = "yes" ]; then
  ARGS="--build-arg JDK25_URL=https://github.com/adoptium/temurin25-binaries/releases/download/jdk-25.0.4.1%2B1/OpenJDK25U-jdk_x64_linux_hotspot_25.0.4.1_1.tar.gz --build-arg JDK25_SHA256=dbb698396d478e7fa2b1e50f4103324b2a99b90569ee27c33f2261f9215cf41e --build-arg GRADLE9_URL=https://services.gradle
fi
rollback() {
  echo "ROLLING BACK to $PREV (files + env from $BK)"
  $SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && tar xzf $BK -C /opt/modbuilder --exclude=root/claudebox.env && tar xzf $BK -C / root/claudebox.env 2>/dev/null; if [ -d /root/.claude-modbuilder.bak-$TS ]; then rm -rf /root/.claude-modbuilder && mv /root/.claude-modbuilder.bak-$TS /root/.claude-modbuilder; fi; ./run
}
if [ "$JDK25" = "yes" ]; then
  $SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && docker build $ARGS --build-arg 'MC26_PINS=$MC26_PINS' -t $TAG . > build-$TS.log 2>&1" || { echo "BUILD FAILED (still on $PREV, nothing restarted):"; $SSH $V "tail -20 /opt/modbuilder/build-$TS.log"; exit 1; }
else
  $SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && docker build -t $TAG . > build-$TS.log 2>&1" || { echo "BUILD FAILED (still on $PREV, nothing restarted):"; $SSH $V "tail -20 /opt/modbuilder/build-$TS.log"; exit 1; }
fi
$SSH $V "cd /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh $TAG" || { rollback; exit 1; }

echo "== 5/7 health: same prompt version, the new image marker (features.catalogTools), auth reported"
ok=0
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 4
  H=$($SSH $V 'curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$H" | grep -q "\"promptVersion\":\"$EXPECT_PROMPT\"" && echo "$H" | grep -q '"catalogTools":true' && { ok=1; break; }
done
echo "$H" | cut -c1-240
if [ $ok -ne 1 ]; then echo "NEW IMAGE NOT HEALTHY"; rollback; exit 1; fi
AUTH=$(echo "$H" | sed -n 's/.*"auth":"\([a-z_]*\)".*/\1/p')
echo "auth: $AUTH   (api_key = paid API key; subscription / subscription_login = the owner's login: NOT for a public launch)"
SCAN_SHA=$(sha256sum "$S/scan.js" | cut -d' ' -f1); REG_SHA=$(sha256sum "$LIBDIR/versions/registry.json" | cut -d' ' -f1)
echo "$H" | grep -q "\"scannerSha256\":\"$SCAN_SHA\"" && echo "hardened scan live (scan.js $SCAN_SHA)" || { echo "SCANNER MISMATCH: the image does not run this scan.js"; rollback; exit 1; }
echo "$H" | grep -q "\"registrySha256\":\"$REG_SHA\"" && echo "registry.json inside the image" || echo "WARN: registry.json missing or different in the image (26.x stays non-buildable)"
echo "$H" | grep -o '"release":{[^}]*}' | cut -c1-300

echo "== 6/7 smoke: an injection-style request must be refused by the guard (one Haiku guard call, a few cents at most)"

#!/bin/bash
# (Re)create the Mod Builder container on the build VM. Idempotent.
#   AUTH, one source of truth. Preferred: ONE Claude login session file (what `claude login` writes to
#   ~/.claude/.credentials.json: access token + refresh token). Keep it in a dedicated directory,
#   CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS_DIR (default /root/.claude-modbuilder), created once with
#     CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/root/.claude-modbuilder claude login
#   (or copy an existing .credentials.json into it). The directory is mounted read-write at /run/claude-auth (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR),
#   outside the CLI user's home and denied to the model's tools, so token refreshes persist and nothing else shares that login. When that file exists the
#   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN line in claudebox.env is ignored (an env token would override the file).
#   WHERE TO EDIT (on the VM): /root/claudebox.env, one KEY=VALUE per line. Any ONE of: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription),
#   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (paid API), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (gateway bearer). Optional gateway: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://host/v1,
#   EXTRA_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=host (the container firewall blocks everything else), MB_MODEL_PREFIX=cc/ (if the gateway namespaces models).
#   Then run this script again to restart the container.
#   Fallback (old way): /root/claudebox.env   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... (owner subscription)  -- or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... for paid API
#   /root/modbuilder.env  MODBUILDER_API_KEY=...      (bearer key the portal uses)
set -euo pipefail
IMAGE="${1:-modbuilder:0.5}"
# Routing / knowledge knobs (see route.js, prompts.js): passed through when set in the caller's env,
# e.g. MB_ROUTING=off /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3  (or put them in /root/modbuilder.env).
PASS=()
for k in MB_ROUTING MB_CLASSIFIER MB_MODEL_SIMPLE MB_MODEL_STANDARD MB_MODEL_COMPLEX MB_REPAIR_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_FIRST MB_REPAIR_SMALL_MAX MB_ROUTE_SIMPLE_MAX MB_ROUTE_COMPLEX_MIN MB_SHEETS MB_RULES MB_MAX_REPAIRS MB_LIVE_STREAM MB_MA
  if [[ -n "${!k:-}" ]]; then PASS+=(-e "$k=${!k}"); fi
done
CRED_DIR="${CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS_DIR:-/root/.claude-modbuilder}"
# Credentials files: defaults are the Nxeon VM layout; override to relocate the service (the entrypoint reads the same env-file).
CLAUDEBOX_ENV="${CLAUDEBOX_ENV:-/root/claudebox.env}"
MODBUILDER_ENV="${MODBUILDER_ENV:-/root/modbuilder.env}"
ENVFILE="$CLAUDEBOX_ENV"
CRED_MOUNT=()
if [[ -f "$CRED_DIR/.credentials.json" ]]; then
  CUID="$(docker run --rm --entrypoint id "$IMAGE" -u claude)"
  chown -R "$CUID:$CUID" "$CRED_DIR"; chmod 700 "$CRED_DIR"; chmod 600 "$CRED_DIR/.credentials.json"
  CRED_MOUNT=(-v "$CRED_DIR:/run/claude-auth" -e CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/run/claude-auth)   # outside $HOME, in a path the model's tools are denied
  ENVFILE=/run/claudebox.nosession.env   # same env file minus the token that would override the login file
  grep -v -E '^(CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN|ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN)=' "$CLAUDEBOX_ENV" > "$ENVFILE" || true
  chmod 600 "$ENVFILE"
  echo "auth: single login session file $CRED_DIR/.credentials.json"
else
  echo "auth: env token from $CLAUDEBOX_ENV (no $CRED_DIR/.credentials.json)"
fi
docker rm -f modbuilder >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker run -d --name modbuilder --restart unless-stopped \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN \
  --env-file "$ENVFILE" --env-file "$MODBUILDER_ENV" ${CRED_MOUNT[@]+"${CRED_MOUNT[@]}"} \
  -e MB_CONCURRENCY="${MB_CONCURRENCY:-2}" -e MB_MODEL="${MB_MODEL:-sonnet}" ${PASS[@]+"${PASS[@]}"} \
  -p 127.0.0.1:7340:3000 \
  -v /var/lib/modbuilder/data:/data -v /var/lib/modbuilder/work:/work \
  --memory 5g --pids-limit 512 \
  "$IMAGE"

# Swap the Claude account the Cyrus build service uses (VM 88001), from PowerShell

Owner runs this. No secrets here: the new account is authorised interactively in your browser, the token never touches chat or git.
Facts (services/modbuilder/run.sh): the container reads ONE login file, `/root/.claude-modbuilder/.credentials.json`
(mounted at /run/claude-auth). Swapping accounts = replace that directory, then `./run.sh <current image>`.
Path: PC -> node-2 `root@178.63.94.114` (jump) -> VM `root@10.20.1.253`. Needs your SSH key for node-2 (same one you use now).
Do it when no build is running (step 1 checks). The restart takes ~15 s; queued builds in flight fail, so pick a quiet moment.

```powershell
$J = "root@178.63.94.114"; $V = "root@10.20.1.253"

# ---- STEP 1: preflight + backup (safe, read-mostly) ----
@'
set -e
echo "== health"; curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | head -c 400; echo
curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | grep -q '"running":0' || { echo "A BUILD IS RUNNING - wait and rerun"; exit 1; }
echo "== image"; docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' modbuilder
TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
cp -a /root/.claude-modbuilder /root/.claude-modbuilder.acctbak-$TS
cp -a /root/claudebox.env /root/claudebox.env.acctbak-$TS
echo "backup suffix: acctbak-$TS"; ls -d /root/.claude-modbuilder.acctbak-*
echo "== is the claude CLI on the VM host?"; command -v claude || echo "no host claude: step 2 will use the container image"
'@ | ssh -J $J $V "bash -s"

# ---- STEP 2: log in as the NEW account (interactive; opens a URL: open it in a browser signed in as the new account, paste the code back) ----
# Uses a separate directory so the live login is untouched until step 3.
ssh -t -J $J $V 'mkdir -p /root/.claude-modbuilder-new && chmod 700 /root/.claude-modbuilder-new && IMG=$(docker inspect -f "{{.Config.Image}}" modbuilder) && if command -v claude >/dev/null; then CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/root/.claude-modbuilder-new claude login; else docker run --rm -it --entrypoint claude -v /root/.claude-modbuilder-new:/cfg -e CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/cfg $IMG login; fi; ls -la /root/.claude-modbuilder-new/.credentials.json'
# The last line must list .credentials.json. If it does not, the login did not finish: rerun step 2.

# ---- STEP 3: swap + restart + verify ----
@'
set -e
curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | grep -q '"running":0' || { echo "A BUILD IS RUNNING - wait and rerun"; exit 1; }
test -s /root/.claude-modbuilder-new/.credentials.json || { echo "no new login file: run step 2"; exit 1; }
IMG=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' modbuilder)
TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
mv /root/.claude-modbuilder /root/.claude-modbuilder.old-$TS
mv /root/.claude-modbuilder-new /root/.claude-modbuilder
cd /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh "$IMG"
for i in $(seq 1 20); do sleep 3; H=$(curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health) && echo "$H" | grep -q '"promptVersion"' && break; done
echo "$H" | head -c 400; echo
echo "$H" | grep -o '"auth":"[a-z_]*"'
echo "old login kept: /root/.claude-modbuilder.old-$TS"
'@ | ssh -J $J $V "bash -s"
# Expect "auth":"subscription_login". Then run ONE cheap real build from the preview account to confirm the new account works.

# ---- ROLLBACK (if health fails or builds error with auth/limit messages) ----
@'
set -e
OLD=$(ls -d /root/.claude-modbuilder.old-* | tail -1)
IMG=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' modbuilder)
mv /root/.claude-modbuilder /root/.claude-modbuilder.failed-$(date +%s)
mv "$OLD" /root/.claude-modbuilder
cd /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh "$IMG"
curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | grep -o '"auth":"[a-z_]*"'
'@ | ssh -J $J $V "bash -s"
```

## Notes
- A subscription login is for your own testing. Before any public launch switch to a paid API key:
  `API_KEY=sk-ant-... bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` on the primary (docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md section 4); `/health` `auth` must read `api_key`.
- Subscription usage limits are shared by everything on that login (all Cyrus builds, evals, flights). The new account's limits apply from now on.
- Cleanup later (after a day of good builds): `rm -rf /root/.claude-modbuilder.old-* /root/.claude-modbuilder.acctbak-*` on the VM (these hold the old account's login: do not leave them forever).

content.content:
### A6. The version selector (registry.json)

Facts (V): `lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json` + `choices.ts`. 1.21.1/4/8/11 = `supported, buildable:true`; 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3 = `preview, buildable:false` and show "Preview: not buildable yet" (`choices.ts:39`). `resourcePackClientVerified:false` on all seven. The registry note says "26.x stays preview until a real-client test passes".

**Why 26.x is preview (V):** (1) the production image has no JDK 25 / Gradle 9 / 26.x classpath built in (Dockerfile ARGs exist, "NOT RUN: no docker build", R0; `/health.versions` lists only 1.21.x); (2) no API sheet for 26.x (`services/modbuilder/sheets/` = 1.21.1/4/8/11 only, `gen-sheets.py` has no 26 branch); (3) no golden plugin or eval run on 26.x (goldens compile `--release 21`, harness 4 versions); (4) no real-client pack check; (5) 26.3 has no stable Paper (only BETA 169), `paperCoordinate:null`.

What already exists for 26.x (V): R0 proof (javac `--release 25` on Temurin 25.0.4.1 against paper-api 26.2.build.133-stable, major 69, scan clean, loaded + enabled on real Paper 26.2, /hellor0 works); classpath script `tools/gen-classpath-26.sh`; exact server pins (26.1.2 build 74, 26.2 build 133 sha256 recorded); pack formats read from server `version.json`; designer/weapons/techniques/creature (BetterModel 3.5.0) flights on 26.2; `javacFor()` already picks JDK 25 when registry marks a 26.x buildable.

**Evidence needed to promote each version (exact):**

| Version | status now | Evidence still missing for `buildable:true` / `supported` | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.11 | supported | real-client pack/texture/sound/HUD check (test-day), paid eval baseline | owner day + about $10-20 U |
| 1.21.8 | supported | same; designer/bot flights only on 1.21.11 (no javac classpath for designer on others, docs/12 3b) | S-M |
| 1.21.4 | supported | same; plus Dialog/menu behaviours | S-M |
| 1.21.1 | supported | same; legacy emitter (`CYRUS_LEGACY_TEXTURES`) unclient-tested; 52-carrier clash | S-M |
| 26.1.2 | preview | (a) image with JDK25+Gradle9+classpath, `MB_VERSIONS` += 26.1.2; (b) 26.x sheet via javap (Adventure 5, registry-interface enums, Brigadier lifecycle) + 26.x failure rules; (c) goldens compiled `--release 25` booted in a flight; (d) one eval set run (coverage 108 + techniques 19) all-pass; (e) real-client pack format 84.0 check; (f) flip registry `buildable:true` + new `registrySha256` in release | L (about 2-4 agent days + about $15-30 U) |
| 26.2 | preview | same as 26.1.2 with pack 88.0 / data 107.1, Adventure 5 removals (`BookMeta`, ClickEvent), beds no longer block entities | L (shared with 26.1.2) |
| 26.3 | preview | blocked: needs a stable Paper build (only BETA exists); then identical list | blocked |

Recommendation (U): do 26.2 only (newest stable), keep 26.1.2 as follow-on, do not touch 26.3. Value is low until users ask: owners "drift to newest fast" (E-versions) so demand will come; cheaper than it looks because designer/creature lanes already fly there.

### A7. Turn-on-now list (ordered, expected effect)

Pre-condition for items 1-2: promote rc3 (devhost build + db push, coach-events SQL, promote, image 0.10). Items marked [now] need no deploy.

| # | Exact switch | Where | Expected effect | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 [now] | `MB_BUILD_BUDGET_USD=1.5`, `MB_CALL_BUDGET_USD=1.0` | build-service env, rerun when no build runs | caps runaway builds at about 750 tokens (U) | low |
| 2 [now] | Setting `cyrus_tok_charge_refused=false`, `cyrus_tok_free_failures=10` | admin Settings | refused/false refusals cost 0; our failures stay free longer | low |
| 3 [now] | `CYRUS_DESIGNER_BUILDS=1` (portal) | env + restart | studio edits become zero-token builds that reach servers | low |
| 4 [after eval, $3] | `MB_TIER_SAKA=claude-sonnet-5-5` | service env | Saka -35..55% cost, 2-3 requests (U) | medium |
| 5 [rc3] | `CYRUS_LEARNING=1` | portal env (+service reads usage) | token/turn capture on new builds; enables path memory, calibrated estimates | none |
| 6 [rc3] | `CYRUS_PERF_WATCH_ACTION=notify` (decision) | worker env | stop auto-disabling customer mods until proven | removes latent risk |
| 7 [rc3 + image] | `CYRUS_PROMPT_COACH=1` after browser check | portal env | fewer vague-prompt rebuilds (23% of spend was rework, V BJ) | low |
| 8 | `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` then `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` | portal/worker env | recipes/loot/enchant/advancement mods become real from one prompt | low-medium |
| 9 [rc3] | `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_WORLDGEN=1`, then `CYRUS_WORLDGEN=1` (after eval) | env | worldgen packs get density probes then are offered | medium |
| 10 [rc3 + image] | `CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES=1` + `MB_MC_TECHNIQUES=1` together | portal + service | vein miner / mob catcher / guns from one prompt | medium |

Turn-on-now list size: **10** (4 usable today without any deploy). Armor, note-block, grip fix and 26.x are deliberately not on it (need a real client).

---

  - There are no 26.x goldens.

# Owner-run helper: set ONE allow-listed platform setting in the production DB, then print the stored value.

content.text:
**Short answer:** it isn't our code. The order was created fine; the failure happened on PayPal's side or the customer's, and we currently can't see the real reason.

## What happened for "Vampire" (new account, PK, Minecraft 4 GB, $8.99), at 16:39 UTC
1. The deploy wizard created the PayPal order. The first attempt, asking to vault the payment method for renewals, was rejected with `NOT_ENABLED_TO_VAULT_PAYMENT_SOURCE`.
2. Our built-in fallback retried without vaulting and succeeded. The order sits in our DB as `PENDING` with a PayPal order id.
3. No capture and no PayPal webhook ever arrived, so the buyer never completed approval in PayPal's popup.
4. The browser's PayPal button then fired its `onError`, which shows the generic "PayPal couldn't complete this payment". The customer also opened card checkout at the same moment and didn't finish it.

## Why I don't think we caused it
- **No PayPal code changed:** the rc3 and portals releases touched none of the PayPal files, and `lib/paypal.ts` was last changed on Aug 29.
- **Same path works for others:** PayPal orders on the same code path were PAID on Oct 1 ($8.99) and Oct 4 ($4.99).
- **Typical abandonment pattern:** PayPal shows 4 paid out of 14 total attempts, and the rest sit `PENDING` with order ids, i.e. buyers who never approved.

## Likely causes (unverified)
- The buyer's PayPal account or funding source declined in the popup. The customer is in Pakistan, where PayPal buyer support is restricted, so that is my first suspect.
- A blocked popup or a closed window.

## Two things worth fixing
1. **Our merchant account isn't vault-enabled.** It isn't the cause here, but it means no saved-PayPal auto-renewals, and every PayPal checkout logs a failed API call first. You can ask PayPal to enable Vault for the account.
2. **The browser swallows the real error.** The generic message hides PayPal's actual reason. I can add a small change that logs the real `onError` detail to the server so this is diagnosable next time.

## For the customer
I haven't contacted them (support rule: no replies without your sign-off). A good suggestion would be paying by card, which they already started, or retrying PayPal with a different funding source. I can draft that reply if you want it.

**Eval and assets agent:** both still running in the background, with 15 of 90 eval builds done, all successful.

# cyrus.my launch: host readiness (PREPARED, NOTHING APPLIED)

Status 2026-10-13, branch `feature/cyrus-portals`. This file only prepares the work: no nginx edit, env write, flag change, DNS, Cloudflare or Stripe change has been made. Every step below is for the owner (or a parent session with the owner's go) to run, in order, with the rollback beside it.

What exists today: the static landing (v7) is live on `cyrus.my` from `/var/www/cyrus.my` (nginx server block `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my`: `/` and `/packs/p/<sha1>.zip` only, no proxy). The app already contains the whole dual-host layer (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE`, `lib/cyrus/bridge/*`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`); it 

## 1. What the app does on cyrus.my (read from code)
Source: `lib/cyrus/bridge/config.ts`, `routing.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `app/cyrus-host/*`, tests `test/cyrus-bridge-routing.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-admin-host.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-portals-routing.test.ts`.

| Public path on cyrus.my | Result |
|---|---|
| `/` | nginx static landing. If it ever reaches the app: 302 `/studio` |
| `/studio[/...]` | rewritten to `/dashboard/cyrus[/...]` (the studio, Cyrus chrome) |
| `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects[/<id>]` | customer app (`/dashboard/cyrus/app/*`), 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off |
| `/help[/<slug>]`, `/plans` | help center and plans page (read-only, 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off) |
| `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/nxeon/start`, `/auth/nxeon/callback`, `/auth/handoff`, `/auth/logout` | Cyrus-host auth pages (`app/cyrus-host/*`, 404 on every other host) |
| `/api/cyrus/*`, `/api/mod-builder/*`, `/api/nxlabs/cyrus*` | the same handlers as on Nxeon |
| `/dashboard/<anything else>` | 302 to the same path on `APP_URL` (Nxeon) |
| `/login`, `/register` | 302 to `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` |
| `/mods/cyrus/*`, `/admin`, `/staff`, `/sso/*`, everything else | 404 |
| `/_next/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/.well-known/*`, `/vendor/*`, static file extensions | pass |

Gaps found while reading, and what to do about them:
1. **Community pages are not served on cyrus.my** (`/mods/cyrus` is a 404 there by design). The generated Featured mods section therefore links to `https://nxeon.cloud/mods/cyrus/<slug>` (`featured.mjs --origin`). If you want them on cyrus.my, that is a routing change plus a test, not a config change.
2. **`/api/cyrus/featured` passes** (prefix `/api/cyrus`). The landing generator reads it at build time; the browser never calls it.
3. nginx must forward only the paths the app serves (section 3) and keep everything else static, otherwise a scanner hits the app for every random path. The app 404s them anyway, so this is load, not safety.
4. The app trusts `X-Real-IP` and the LAST `X-Forwarded-For` hop; with Cloudflare in front, nginx must restore the real visitor IP (`deploy/cloudflare`, already built) or rate limits see Cloudflare's addresses.
5. No WebSocket path is exposed on cyrus.my (the Nxeon terminal and console sockets stay on nxeon.cloud). The `Upgrade` headers in the block below are copied from the Nxeon block and are harmless.

## 2. Environment (names only; set in the app's env file on the primary, then restart `nxeon-web`)
| Variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` | `1` | master switch; unset = nothing changes for any request |
| `CYRUS_HOSTS` | `cyrus.my,www.cyrus.my` (default) | exact hostnames that get Cyrus chrome; first entry is the apex |
| `CYRUS_ORIGIN` | `https://cyrus.my` (default) | callback and return base |
| `APP_URL` | `https://nxeon.cloud` (already set) | the Nxeon origin: identity provider, wallet, `/dashboard/*` hand-over |
| `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` | `1` | customer app + help center + plans (also needs the studio gate) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST` | `<16-63 [a-z0-9]>.cyrus.my` | secret admin host (kept ONLY in env and the password manager) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_IPS` | optional exact staff IPs | other IPs get 404 (reads `X-Real-IP`) |
| `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY` | `1` only after the admin host works | `/admin/cyrus` 404s on every other host |
| `CYRUS_BRIDGE_REQUIRE_VERIFIED` | leave default (strict) | Cyrus sign-in needs a verified email |
| `CYRUS_WALLET_PAY` | `1` if wallet top-ups should work from cyrus.my | optional |
| `ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_API_KEY` | optional | Economy tab live Anthropic costs (server only; not needed for launch) |

Session and SSO: no setting to change. The Cyrus session cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` (Secure, path `/`, no Domain, so it cannot be shared with or set from another host); SSO state cookies are `__Host-*_sso_state`; the callback URLs are the exact strings `https://cyrus.my/auth/nxeon/callback` and `https://nxeon.cloud/sso/cyr

Also keep the pre-launch pair consistent (`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` and `cyrus_tok_live`, the smoke script checks it) and `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` for the community and featured API.

49	## 3. nginx additions (EXACT; add to the existing HTTPS block of `cyrus-my`, nothing else touched)
50	The static pieces stay: `location = /`, `/packs/`, and `location /` with `try_files`. Add one named location and proxy locations for the app paths. `nxeon_web` is the upstream already defined in `conf.d/nxeon-web-upstream.conf` and used by `nxeon-cloud`.
51	
52	```nginx
53	# --- inside the existing `server { listen 443 ssl; server_name cyrus.my www.cyrus.my; ... }` ---
54	    client_max_body_size 20m;                 # attachments / images in the studio (same order as nxeon-cloud)
55	    error_page 502 503 504 /maintenance.html;
56	    location = /maintenance.html { root /opt/nxeon/public; internal; }
57	
58	    # app paths: proxied to the SAME backend as nxeon.cloud
59	    location ~ ^/(studio|home|new|account|projects|help|plans|sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register|dashboard|api/cyrus|api/mod-builder|api/nxlabs/cyrus|_next|vendor)(/|$) {
60	        proxy_pass http://nxeon_web;
61	        proxy_http_version 1.1;
62	        proxy_set_header Host $host;
63	        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
64	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
65	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
66	        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
67	        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
68	        proxy_read_timeout 600s;              # builds stream for minutes
69	        proxy_send_timeout 600s;
70	        proxy_buffering off;                  # live build streams (SSE) must not be buffered
71	    }
72	    # the favicon and the app's well-known files come from the app, not the static root
73	    location = /favicon.ico { proxy_pass http://nxeon_web; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; }
74	```
75	Notes:
76	- The landing's own assets live under `/assets/` and `/fonts`-style paths inside the static root; none of them collide with the regexp (`_next` and `vendor` are app-only).
77	- `/.well-known/acme-challenge/` stays on the HTTP block (certbot). Do not proxy `/.well-known/` on 443.
78	- Rate limits: reuse the zones the Nxeon block uses for `/login`: add `limit_req zone=nxeon_auth burst=15 nodelay;` inside a separate `location ~ ^/(sign-in|sign-up|auth|login|register)(/|$)` copy of the block above (the zone is defined in `conf.d/nxeon-security.conf`).
79	- Validate before reload: `nginx -t`; reload with `systemctl reload nginx` (no restart).
80	- A staging check without DNS: `curl -sk --resolve cyrus.my:443:<origin IP> https://cyrus.my/studio -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'`.
81	
82	## 4. Cloudflare (zone `cyrus.my`)
83	1. SSL/TLS mode **Full (strict)** (the origin has a real Let's Encrypt certificate; the temporary self-signed one must be gone first: `openssl s_client -connect <primary public IP>:443 -servername cyrus.my | openssl x509 -noout -issuer`).
84	2. Always Use HTTPS on; minimum TLS 1.2; HSTS only after one week of clean traffic.
85	3. Real visitor IP: install `deploy/cloudflare/nginx` (CF-Connecting-IP -> `real_ip`) and the `cf-ips-update` timer BEFORE the app paths are proxied. Verify with the simulation test `test/cloudflare-realip.test.ts` and a request to `/api/cyrus/health`.
86	4. Cache rules (start from `deploy/cloudflare/cache-rules.json`; the list below is what this launch needs): cache `/assets/*`, `/_next/static/*`, `/packs/p/*` (immutable); **bypass** `/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/studio*`, `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects*`, `/help*`, `/plans` and any request with the `__Host-cyrus_session` cookie. Never cache HTML of the app paths.
87	5. WAF: managed ruleset on; a rate-limiting rule of about 20 requests/min per IP on `/auth/*` and `/sign-in`; leave bot fight mode off for `/api/*` (the build stream and the API clients are not browsers). Do not enable "Rocket Loader" or "Email Obfuscation" (they rewrite the app's HTML).
88	6. WebSockets: not used on these paths. Live build streams are plain HTTP; Cloudflare closes a connection idle for about 100 s, so UNVERIFIED: confirm during the smoke that a long build's live view keeps updating (the studio polls and reconnects).
89	7. The secret admin host: its own proxied A record + Origin CA certificate (`deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md`); never a per-host Let's Encrypt certificate.
90	
91	## 5. Stripe (same account as Nxeon)
92	- Checkouts opened on cyrus.my are embedded Stripe Checkout sessions whose `return_url` is `https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/tokens/return?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` (storage add-on: `/api/cyrus/storage/return?...`), built from `returnBase`. Embedded checkout needs no return-URL allowlist.
93	- Dashboard: register `cyrus.my` (and `www.cyrus.my`) under Settings > Payment method domains (Apple Pay / Google Pay), same account.
94	- Webhook endpoint stays ONE (`https://nxeon.cloud/api/stripe/webhook`); fulfilment is idempotent and does not depend on the host. No new endpoint, no new secret.
95	- Customer portal / billing deep links open on nxeon.cloud (`/dashboard/*` hand-over). Plan prices in the Economy tab are display values; the charge is the Stripe Price.
96	- Test in test mode first: a card checkout, the return page, the token credit, then the same with the wallet (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`).
97	
98	## 6. Order of work (each step reversible; stop at the first failure)
99	1. Land the branch; deploy with every Cyrus switch as today (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` unset). Nothing changes.
100	2. Cloudflare real-IP + SSL Full (strict) + cert check (section 4.1, 4.3).
101	3. Set env (section 2) but keep `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` unset; restart `nxeon-web`.
102	4. nginx: add section 3 to a copy, `nginx -t`, reload.
103	5. Smoke (section 7). Then `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP=1`, smoke again.
104	6. Admin host (separate runbook), then `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` last.
105	7. Publish the updated landing with `CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON` only when `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` is on and mods are featured.
106	
107	## 7. Smoke tests (read-only)
108	```
109	bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh flags     # launch pair consistent, switch combinations, env names (values hidden)
110	bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service   # build service reachable, auth api_key before any public launch
111	bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh worker    # nxeon-web / nxeon-worker active, no recent cyrus errors
112	bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh migrations
113	```
114	Plus HTTP checks (from outside, through Cloudflare):
115	| Request | Expect |
116	|---|---|
117	| `GET https://cyrus.my/` | 200, the static landing (same `ETag` as before) |
118	| `GET https://cyrus.my/packs/p/<known sha1>.zip` | 200 `application/zip`, immutable |
119	| `GET https://cyrus.my/studio` (signed out) | 302 to `/sign-in...` |
120	| `GET https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | 200 |
121	| `GET https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | 200 JSON |
122	| `GET https://cyrus.my/admin`, `/staff`, `/mods/cyrus`, `/random` | 404 |
123	| `GET https://cyrus.my/dashboard/servers` | 302 to `https://nxeon.cloud/dashboard/servers` |
124	| `GET https://cyrus.my/home` | 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off, 200 or sign-in redirect after |
125	| `curl -I https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | no `Set-Cookie` without a sign-in; later cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` |
126	| Sign in with Nxeon end to end | lands on `/studio`; Nxeon cookie NOT set on cyrus.my |
127	| `GET https://<admin-host>/` | 302 `/admin/cyrus` (staff only) |
128	
129	## 8. Rollback
130	- nginx: restore the saved copy of `cyrus-my` (`cp cyrus-my.bak cyrus-my && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`). The landing and packs are untouched by the additions, so rollback is instant and static-only again.
131	- App: unset `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` (and `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`), restart `nxeon-web`: the app answers as if cyrus.my did not exist. Nxeon is unaffected throughout (separate cookie, separate hostname).
132	- Landing: `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh rollback` (atomic symlink back to the previous release).
133	- Cloudflare: revert the cache and WAF rules you added; keep SSL Full (strict). Switching records to DNS-only exposes the origin IP and is a last resort.
134	- Data: nothing here writes or migrates data; the only new setting key is `cyrus_featured_pages`, `cyrus_econ_*` (projection inputs) and these can stay.

3. Real visitor IP: install `deploy/cloudflare/nginx` (CF-Connecting-IP -> `real_ip`) and the `cf-ips-update` timer BEFORE the app paths are proxied. Verify with the simulation test `test/cloudflare-realip.test.ts` and a request to `/api/cyrus/health`.
4. Cache rules (start from `deploy/cloudflare/cache-rules.json`; the list below is what this launch needs): cache `/assets/*`, `/_next/static/*`, `/packs/p/*` (immutable); **bypass** `/api/*`, `/auth/*`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/studio*`, `/home`, `/new`, `/account`, `/projects*`, `/help*`, `/plans` and any request with the `__Host-cyrus_session` cookie. Never cache HTML of the app paths.
5. WAF: managed ruleset on; a rate-limiting rule of about 20 requests/min per IP on `/auth/*` and `/sign-in`; leave bot fight mode off for `/api/*` (the build stream and the API clients are not browsers). Do not enable "Rocket Loader" or "Email Obfuscation" (they rewrite the app's HTML).
6. WebSockets: not used on these paths. Live build streams are plain HTTP; Cloudflare closes a connection idle for about 100 s, so UNVERIFIED: confirm during the smoke that a long build's live view keeps updating (the studio polls and reconnects).
7. The secret admin host: its own proxied A record + Origin CA certificate (`deploy/cyrus/CYRUS-ADMIN-HOST.md`); never a per-host Let's Encrypt certificate.

## 5. Stripe (same account as Nxeon)
- Checkouts opened on cyrus.my are embedded Stripe Checkout sessions whose `return_url` is `https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/tokens/return?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` (storage add-on: `/api/cyrus/storage/return?...`), built from `returnBase`. Embedded checkout needs no return-URL allowlist.
- Dashboard: register `cyrus.my` (and `www.cyrus.my`) under Settings > Payment method domains (Apple Pay / Google Pay), same account.
- Webhook endpoint stays ONE (`https://nxeon.cloud/api/stripe/webhook`); fulfilment is idempotent and does not depend on the host. No new endpoint, no new secret.
- Customer portal / billing deep links open on nxeon.cloud (`/dashboard/*` hand-over). Plan prices in the Economy tab are display values; the charge is the Stripe Price.
- Test in test mode first: a card checkout, the return page, the token credit, then the same with the wallet (`CYRUS_WALLET_PAY`).

## 6. Order of work (each step reversible; stop at the first failure)
1. Land the branch; deploy with every Cyrus switch as today (`CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` unset). Nothing changes.
2. Cloudflare real-IP + SSL Full (strict) + cert check (section 4.1, 4.3).
3. Set env (section 2) but keep `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` unset; restart `nxeon-web`.
4. nginx: add section 3 to a copy, `nginx -t`, reload.
5. Smoke (section 7). Then `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP=1`, smoke again.
6. Admin host (separate runbook), then `CYRUS_ADMIN_HOST_ONLY=1` last.
7. Publish the updated landing with `CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON` only when `cyrus_mods_public_enabled` is on and mods are featured.

## 7. Smoke tests (read-only)
```
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh flags     # launch pair consistent, switch combinations, env names (values hidden)
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh service   # build service reachable, auth api_key before any public launch
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh worker    # nxeon-web / nxeon-worker active, no recent cyrus errors
bash scripts/cyrus/smoke-readonly.sh migrations
```
Plus HTTP checks (from outside, through Cloudflare):
| Request | Expect |
|---|---|
| `GET https://cyrus.my/` | 200, the static landing (same `ETag` as before) |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/packs/p/<known sha1>.zip` | 200 `application/zip`, immutable |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/studio` (signed out) | 302 to `/sign-in...` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | 200 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | 200 JSON |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/admin`, `/staff`, `/mods/cyrus`, `/random` | 404 |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/dashboard/servers` | 302 to `https://nxeon.cloud/dashboard/servers` |
| `GET https://cyrus.my/home` | 404 while `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP` is off, 200 or sign-in redirect after |
| `curl -I https://cyrus.my/sign-in` | no `Set-Cookie` without a sign-in; later cookie is `__Host-cyrus_session` |
| Sign in with Nxeon end to end | lands on `/studio`; Nxeon cookie NOT set on cyrus.my |
| `GET https://<admin-host>/` | 302 `/admin/cyrus` (staff only) |

## 8. Rollback
- nginx: restore the saved copy of `cyrus-my` (`cp cyrus-my.bak cyrus-my && nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`). The landing and packs are untouched by the additions, so rollback is instant and static-only again.
- App: unset `CYRUS_DOMAIN_MODE` (and `CYRUS_CUSTOMER_APP`), restart `nxeon-web`: the app answers as if cyrus.my did not exist. Nxeon is unaffected throughout (separate cookie, separate hostname).
- Landing: `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh rollback` (atomic symlink back to the previous release).
- Cloudflare: revert the cache and WAF rules you added; keep SSL Full (strict). Switching records to DNS-only exposes the origin IP and is a last resort.
- Data: nothing here writes or migrates data; the only new setting key is `cyrus_featured_pages`, `cyrus_econ_*` (projection inputs) and these can stay.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

</system-reminder>

**It's done and working.** The 404s I saw a minute ago were the app still warming up right after the restart. Checked again through Cloudflare and directly at the origin:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `cyrus.my/` | 200, static landing |
| `cyrus.my/sign-in` | 200 |
| `cyrus.my/api/cyrus/health` | 200 |
| `cyrus.my/studio` | 307, redirects to sign-in |
| `cyrus.my/dashboard/servers` | 302, hands over to nxeon.cloud |
| `cyrus.my/admin`, `/mods/cyrus` | 404 (intended) |

nginx, web, and worker are all active, and `nxeon.cloud` is unaffected. You can try it now: open **https://cyrus.my/sign-in** and use "Sign in with Nxeon".

## Stripe: you don't need to do anything
- **Same key:** it already uses the same Stripe account and API key as Nxeon. Payments from cyrus.my work with no change.
- **Domain registration:** that's a separate, optional Stripe feature that only enables the **Apple Pay and Google Pay** buttons on that domain. Card payments work without it.
- **Your case:** you probably never noticed it on Nxeon because those wallet buttons just don't appear unless the domain is registered. Skip it unless you want those buttons.

## Cloudflare in plain English
Cloudflare sits in front of cyrus.my and passes traffic to your server. Of my list, only the first matters:

| Setting | What it means | Do you need it? |
|---|---|---|
| **SSL mode "Full (strict)"** | How Cloudflare talks to your server. "Full (strict)" checks your server's certificate is real, which yours is. | One click (SSL/TLS → Overview → Full (strict)). It works as is, this is just the safest setting. |
| **Cache rules** | Cloudflare doesn't cache dynamic pages by default, only static files. | No. Skip unless you ever created a "Cache Everything" rule. |
| **WAF rate limit** | Slows password-guessing on sign-in. | Optional: nginx already rate-limits the sign-in paths. |
| **Rocket Loader / Email Obfuscation** | Off by default. They rewrite page code and would break the app if on. | Only check they're off (Speed → Optimization). |

## What's left for cyrus.my
- **Admin host (optional):** the secret subdomain for the admin needs its own DNS record and Origin CA cert. Until then the Cyrus admin lives at `/admin/cyrus` on your Nxeon admin host.
- **Public launch:** the public switches are still off, so only your preview account can use the studio.
