Everything promoted so far is live and healthy: `nxeon.cloud` and `cyrus.my/sign-in` both return 200.

## Done
| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Assets catalogue and SFX play buttons | **Live**, promoted with no schema change |
| cyrus.my host | Live, all smoke checks pass |
| Cloudflare | Nothing needed from you |
| Eval `first1` | Running |

## Cloudflare, settled
- **My checks:** I verified from outside, since the server's token is DNS-only and can't change zone settings. App pages are uncached and unrewritten, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over HTTPS.
- **Tiny gap:** typing `http://cyrus.my/sign-in` by hand gives a 404, because the port-80 nginx block is static-only. The classifier denied my fix as "Modify Shared Resources", so I'm leaving it. Real traffic uses HTTPS links, so this is cosmetic.

## Eval, what it's telling us so far
- **Progress:** 34 of 90 done, 33 succeeded, and every one that built also booted on a real server.
- **One refusal:** `ast-music-disc` was refused by the guard at $0.002, which looks like the guard doing its job.
- **Cost:** about $10.09 spent, and asset builds average about $0.55–0.85 each versus $0.04–0.20 for plain builds, so the runner's $22 cap will stop it before the remaining 56 builds.
- **What that means:** I'll treat the partial baseline as the first honest measurement, and the report will say which lanes got covered. Asset builds cost about 4× more than the plan-screen estimate assumes.

## Next, and what needs your hands
1. **When the eval stops:** I read `report.md` and summarise it. Then I run the 19-prompt techniques set.
2. **Technique flags:** restarting the build service with `MB_MC_TECHNIQUES` and flipping `CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES` both need the build service idle, which happens once the eval finishes. I'll do the VM side myself, and the portal flag write is the one thing that has been denied in the past.
3. **Remaining blocked item:** `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED` is a licence decision, not a technical one. I won't flip it without your explicit call.

1	# Cyrus owner test deploy (release candidate rc1)
2	
3	Written 2026-10-11 by the rc1 agent on `release/cyrus-rc1` (= `feature/cyrus-r2` + `main` e62aa07c6d + `feature/cyrus-r49-qa` parts 1-4). If r49 part 5 or new main commits land first, merge them into this branch and re-run the suite and `npm run build` on node-2 before step 1. **Nothing here has been run on production.** The parent/owner runs it, one step at a time, on the primary, in a quiet hour. After each step: run its smoke, read it, go on only when it is clean. Every step has its own rollback.
4	
5	Goal: the owner tests Minecraft mods with **textures, sounds, item models (item states) and designers** on his own server, as the only preview account. Every public switch stays OFF. The full background runbook is [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md](CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md); this page is the owner-test subset, with the exact values.
6	
7	## Facts this plan is built on (from the 2026-10-11 03:17 backup, restored to a throwaway DB, read-only)
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| Preview account | `nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com` (user `cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi`, role CUSTOMER, not suspended). No `preview_access_emails*` Setting row exists, so `lib/preview-access.ts` falls back to `DEFAULT_PREVIEW_EMAILS` = this account. **Nothing to add.** Do NOT create a `preview_access_emails` row unless you want to change the list: a row replaces the default. |
12	| Cyrus usage in prod | No `cyrus_*` Setting row at all (every setting = its default, the launch pair is off). One `CyrusTokenAccount` (the owner, `tierOverride=all`), zero `CyrusPlan` rows, 17 builds, all by the owner. |
13	| Test server | `minecraft-f3izjh` (label "My server"), id `cmuzuj8wl00xshlv49mfv4a1p`, **owned by the preview account** (no grant or ownership change needed). Paper **1.21.11**, `MEMORY=4G`, online-mode false. Plan "Minecraft 4 GB / 20 slots" (4096 MB, 2 cores, 30 GB). VM 88006 on **node-7** (`nxeon-sgp4`, OVH SGP), guest 10.20.6.101, join `139.99.125.190:20117`. RUNNING. Three earlier Cyrus mods are installed and DISABLED (Handgun9mm 1.0.0, Banshee 1.2.0, RandomDrops 1.3.0). |
14	| Build target | **Minecraft 1.21.11 (Paper)**: the server's version and the most-verified lane (Test Flight classpath, item model definitions, sounds, designers). No 26.x needed, so no `JDK25=yes`. |
15	| RAM | Pack Loader is a 12 KB plugin; the resource pack is downloaded by the client from `cyrus.my`, not held by the server. Extra server memory is negligible. Note: the heap (`MEMORY=4G`) already equals the VM's 4096 MB; that is today's setting, not caused by this release. Look at the panel's RAM graph before the test. |
16	| How delivery reaches node-7 | The same path as today's Cyrus installs: the worker on the primary opens the guest through the Mods engine (`ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS=1`, already on) and writes `/opt/mc/plugins`. With `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` the same Install also places Pack Loader (from `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGIN_DIR` on the primary) and its pack config (pack URL + sha1). |

28	## 1. Code: fast-forward main, then the database, then promote (all switches off)

31

34	```

37	
38	**1b. Manual SQL, before the promote** (rehearsed on the restored backup; each file ran in under 0.2 s, all inside one transaction each):
39	
40	```
41	URL="$(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')"
42	cd /opt/nxeon
43	for f in 2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core 2026-10-10-cyrus-managed-plugins 2026-10-10-cyrus-catalog-v2 \
44	         2026-10-10-cyrus-library-backend 2026-10-11-cyrus-model-drafts 2026-10-11-cyrus-legal-cases \

47	done

If the production role may not create it, that file fails and rolls back by itself: then skip it and go on (db push creates its tables; the two GIN indexes can be added later; nothing reads them while `CYRUS_LIBRARY_BACKEND` is off).

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

#!/bin/bash
# Cyrus real-client test day, owner side (run from a worktree on the primary, never /opt/nxeon). Everything heavy runs on
# node-2 through scripts/devhost; nothing here spends model money or touches a customer server.
#   scripts/cyrus/testday.sh build                      build the kit on node-2 (packs + compiled showcase plugins + CHECKLIST.md + results.json)
#   scripts/cyrus/testday.sh fetch [DIR]                copy the kit (CHECKLIST.md, results.json, READMEs) to DIR (default ./testday-kit)
#   scripts/cyrus/testday.sh start <version> <mc-name>  start the throwaway server for one version and print how to connect
#   scripts/cyrus/testday.sh logs | stop                server log / stop it (one version at a time)
#   scripts/cyrus/testday.sh ingest <results.json> [--apply]   verdict per version; --apply writes registry.json + client-verify.json here
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
case "$PWD" in /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging) echo "testday: run this from a worktree, not $PWD" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
DEVHOST="${DEVHOST:-/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost}"
KIT="${TESTDAY_KIT:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testday/kit}"
HOST="${CYRUS_BUILD_HOST:-root@178.63.94.114}"
MC_PORT="${TESTDAY_MC_PORT:-25599}"; HTTP_PORT="${TESTDAY_HTTP_PORT:-8799}"
case "${1:-}" in
  build) "$DEVHOST" run --lock --max 1200 -- npx tsx scripts/cyrus/testday-kit.ts build --out "$KIT" --compile ;;
  fetch) mkdir -p "${2:-./testday-kit}"; rsync -a --exclude=src/ -e "ssh -o BatchMode=yes" "$HOST:$KIT/" "${2:-./testday-kit}/" && echo "kit in ${2:-./testday-kit} (CHECKLIST.md, results.json, READMEs
  start)
    VER="${2:?version}"; NAME="${3:?your Minecraft Java name}"
    "$DEVHOST" stop testday >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$DEVHOST" bg testday -- env TESTDAY_MC_PORT="$MC_PORT" TESTDAY_HTTP_PORT="$HTTP_PORT" bash scripts/cyrus/testday-serve.sh "$VER" "$NAME" "$KIT"
    cat <<MSG

Test day server for Minecraft $VER is starting (about 30-60 s; 'scripts/cyrus/testday.sh logs' shows "Done").
On the computer with Minecraft Java $VER, open a terminal and keep this running:

  ssh -N -L 25565:127.0.0.1:$MC_PORT -L $HTTP_PORT:127.0.0.1:$HTTP_PORT $HOST

Then in Minecraft: Multiplayer > Direct Connection > localhost   (you are op; the pack prompt appears on join)
Checklist: CHECKLIST.md in the kit ('scripts/cyrus/testday.sh fetch'). Stop with 'scripts/cyrus/testday.sh stop'.
MSG
    ;;
  logs) "$DEVHOST" logs testday -n "${2:-80}" ;;
  stop) "$DEVHOST" stop testday ;;
  ingest)
    RES="${2:?results.json}"; APPLY="${3:-}"
    cp -f "$RES" .testday-results.json
    "$DEVHOST" run -- npx tsx scripts/cyrus/testday-kit.ts ingest --kit "$KIT" --results .testday-results.json $APPLY
    rm -f .testday-results.json

#!/bin/bash
# Cyrus test day: ONE throwaway Paper server for a real Minecraft client. Runs ON node-2 (started by
# scripts/cyrus/testday.sh start, inside devhost's capped agent slice as a background unit). Not Test Flight (that
# one has no network by design): this binds 127.0.0.1 only, online mode, whitelisted + op for ONE tester, flat world,
# and serves the kit's resource pack on 127.0.0.1 so the client reaches both through one SSH tunnel.
#   testday-serve.sh <version> <minecraft-name> [kit-dir]
# Stopped by `testday.sh stop` (systemctl stop of the unit = the whole cgroup: java + the pack server). Never pkill.
set -euo pipefail
VER="${1:?version}"; NAME="${2:?minecraft name}"; KIT="${3:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testday/kit}"
case "$NAME" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_]*|"") echo "bad Minecraft name" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
TF="${CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_ROOT:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight}"
MC_PORT="${TESTDAY_MC_PORT:-25599}"; HTTP_PORT="${TESTDAY_HTTP_PORT:-8799}"
SHA=$(node -e 'const r=require(process.argv[2]).versions.find((v)=>v.id===process.argv[1]); if(!r||!r.paperServerSha256){process.exit(3)} console.log(r.paperServerSha256)' "$VER" "$PWD/lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json") || { echo "no pinned Paper server for $VER in the registry" >&2; exit 3; }
PAPER="$TF/paper/$SHA"
[ -f "$PAPER/paper.jar" ] || { echo "no cached Paper $VER at $PAPER: run one Test Flight on $VER first (it downloads + verifies the jar)" >&2; exit 3; }
[ -f "$KIT/$VER/pack.zip" ] || { echo "no kit for $VER in $KIT: run testday.sh build first" >&2; exit 3; }
SRV="$(dirname "$KIT")/servers/$VER"
mkdir -p "$SRV/plugins"
find "$SRV/plugins" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.jar' -delete
cp -f "$KIT/$VER/plugins/"*.jar "$SRV/plugins/" 2>/dev/null || echo "note: no compiled plugins for $VER (pack steps only)"
SHA1=$(sha1sum "$KIT/$VER/pack.zip" | cut -d' ' -f1)
RAW=$(curl -fsS --max-time 15 "https://api.mojang.com/users/profiles/minecraft/$NAME") || { echo "Mojang has no Java profile named $NAME" >&2; exit 4; }
UUID=$(printf '%s' "$RAW" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; i=json.load(sys.stdin)["id"]; print(f"{i[:8]}-{i[8:12]}-{i[12:16]}-{i[16:20]}-{i[20:]}")')
cd "$SRV"
rm -rf -- "$SRV/world" "$SRV/world_nether" "$SRV/world_the_end"   # a fresh world every start
printf '[{"uuid":"%s","name":"%s","level":4,"bypassesPlayerLimit":false}]\n' "$UUID" "$NAME" > ops.json
printf '[{"uuid":"%s","name":"%s"}]\n' "$UUID" "$NAME" > whitelist.json
echo "eula=true" > eula.txt
cat > server.properties <<PROPS
server-ip=127.0.0.1
server-port=$MC_PORT
online-mode=true
white-list=true
enforce-whitelist=true
max-players=4
level-type=minecraft\:flat
generator-settings={"layers":[{"block":"minecraft:bedrock","height":1},{"block":"minecraft:dirt","height":2},{"block":"minecraft:grass_block","height":1}],"biome":"minecraft:plains"}
spawn-protection=0
view-distance=6
simulation-distance=6
enable-rcon=false
motd=Cyrus test day $VER
resource-pack=http\://127.0.0.1\:$HTTP_PORT/$VER/pack.zip
resource-pack-sha1=$SHA1
require-resource-pack=true

1. Open **https://cyrus.my/sign-in** and use "Sign in with Nxeon" with your preview account (`nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com`).

> Banshee boss: a pale hooded vex-based enemy that spawns with /banshee, with a custom texture for its summoning item (a ghostly lantern) and four custom sounds (wail, scream, hurt, death). Drains hearts when near. Needs a boss bar.

Listen for the four sounds, and report whether they play and whether they sound right.

- **To help me:** tell me what the plan screen showed and anything that looked off, such as the coach panel, the token cost, or the SFX play buttons.

Here's what I found for each issue, what I've started, and the one thing I need you to paste.

## 1. Planning has taken over 2 minutes
**Cause:** it isn't planning, it's queueing. The build service has 2 slots and the eval is occupying both. Your build is queued at position 1 and starts as soon as an eval build finishes (they run 1–2 minutes each). It should already be running. If it's still stuck in a couple of minutes, tell me and I'll pause the eval so your build gets a slot.

**Real fix, noted for later:** interactive builds should never wait behind batch evals. I'll add a reserved slot or priority to the build service.

## 2. No images on cyrus.my
**Cause:** the landing's own images are fine (23 of 23 return 200). What's broken is the app's images, such as the Cyrus wordmark and the icons on sign-in and studio pages. They live in the app's `public/` folder, and my nginx rules only proxied a fixed list of paths, so those requests 404'd.

**Fix** (the classifier denied my attempt, so it needs your paste). It lets any path that isn't a static landing file fall through to the app, adds an HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, and reverts automatically if `nginx -t` fails:
```bash
F=$(readlink -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/cyrus-my); TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S); cp -a "$F" /root/cyrus-my.nginx.bak-fallback-$TS && python3 - "$F" <<'PY'
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
if '@cyrus_app' in s: print('already patched'); sys.exit(0)
m='    location / { try_files $uri $uri/ =404; }'
first=s.find(m); last=s.rfind(m)
assert first>0 and last>first, 'anchors'
named='''    # CYRUS_APP_FALLBACK: anything that is not a static landing file is served by the app
    location @cyrus_app {
        proxy_pass http://nxeon_web;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
    location / { try_files $uri $uri/ @cyrus_app; }'''
s=s[:last]+named+s[last+len(m):]
s=s[:first]+'    location / { return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }'+s[first+len(m):]
open(p,'w').write(s); print('patched')
PY
nginx -t 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -q successful && systemctl reload nginx && echo reloaded || { cp -a /root/cyrus-my.nginx.bak-fallback-$TS "$F"; echo "nginx -t failed: restored"; }
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "wordmark %{http_code}\n" https://cyrus.my/cyrus/brand/wordmark-dark.webp; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "icon %{http_code}\n" https://cyrus.my/icon-192.png
```
Expect `wordmark 200` and `icon 200`.

## 3. "Sign in" on the marketing page says it's a demo
**Cause:** those three buttons in the static landing are demo stubs, not real links.
**Fix:** the agent wires them to `/sign-in` and `/sign-up`. It's a static file, so after it lands I'll need to publish it with `apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh`, and I'll try that myself.

## 4. Wallet / My servers links go to Nxeon pages
**Cause:** the Cyrus top bar hard-codes `nxeon.cloud/dashboard/servers` and `/dashboard/billing`.
**Fix, in the same agent:** it builds Cyrus-native **Servers** and **Wallet** pages on cyrus.my. They include the install actions, token and wallet top-up, and history. Anything that truly only exists on Nxeon (console, files) opens in a new tab and says "on Nxeon".

I'll verify the branch (tsc, the full suite, the flights) when the agent reports, then promote it.

That's a flag write, so it's the one thing you need to paste. Here's a single batch for both sides, and the techniques pair goes in at the same time since both need a restart anyway:

```bash
bash -s <<'BATCH'
set -u
TS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
# 1. build service (VM 88001): only when idle
ssh -o BatchMode=yes -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253 'curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | grep -q "\"running\":0" || { echo "BUILD RUNNING on the VM: rerun in a minute"; exit 1; }
cp -a /root/modbuilder.env /root/modbuilder.env.bak-live-$(date +%s)
sed -i "/^CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS=/d;/^MB_MC_TECHNIQUES=/d" /root/modbuilder.env
printf "CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS=1\nMB_MC_TECHNIQUES=1\n" >> /root/modbuilder.env
IMG=$(docker inspect -f "{{.Config.Image}}" modbuilder); cd /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh "$IMG" >/dev/null; sleep 6
curl -s 127.0.0.1:7340/health | grep -o -E "\"(auth|liveStream)\":[^,]*" | tr "\n" " "; echo
docker exec modbuilder printenv CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS MB_MC_TECHNIQUES | tr "\n" " "' || exit 1
# 2. portal env + one restart of the web app (about 40 s of 502s)
cp -a /opt/nxeon/.env /opt/nxeon/.env.bak-live-$TS
sed -i '/^CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS=/d;/^CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES=/d' /opt/nxeon/.env
printf 'CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS=1\nCYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES=1\n' >> /opt/nxeon/.env
systemctl restart nxeon-web
for i in $(seq 1 30); do c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 5 https://nxeon.cloud/); [ "$c" = 200 ] && break; sleep 3; done
echo "nxeon.cloud $c; web: $(systemctl is-active nxeon-web)"
BATCH
```

**What it enables**
- **`CYRUS_LIVE_ASSETS` (both sides):** the live build view shows the texture being drawn, sounds being picked, and the code being written while the build runs.
- **Techniques pair (`CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES` + `MB_MC_TECHNIQUES`):** vein miner, mob catcher and guns become buildable from one prompt.
- **Rollback:** restore the backups it creates (`/root/modbuilder.env.bak-live-*` on the VM, `/opt/nxeon/.env.bak-live-*` on the primary) and restart.

**Then:** run another build (the Ruby Sword prompt again) and you should see the live canvas.

content.content:
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.

content.text:
## First real numbers on how well Cyrus works

I stopped guessing and measured it. This is 59 real builds on Minecraft 1.21.11 at the Saka tier, each booted on a real Paper server.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Builds that ended up working | **98.3%** |
| Booted cleanly on a real server | **100% (58 of 58)** |
| Worked on the first try | **57.6%** |
| Cost per working build | $0.34 |
| Plain plugins / designers / textures / sounds | $0.15 / $0.37 / $0.50 / $0.49 |

**The problem is the first try, and that's what costs money.**
- 42% of builds needed a repair.
- Those repairs consumed 65% of the total spend ($12.76 of $19.56).
- A retried build costs about twice a clean one.
- The plan-screen estimate was exceeded for 13 of 15 texture builds, 6 of 6 sound builds, and 11 of 18 designer builds.

**What triggers the repairs (the fix list):**
1. **Performance pre-check:** 9 builds (spawning in a loop and the like).
2. **"No design found":** 7 builds, where the model wrote no design file for the lane it was supposed to use.
3. **Sound check problems:** 5 builds.
4. **Design check and compile errors:** 7 builds.
5. **Quality misses:** the handgun sounds and the handgun texture scored low, "music disc" was falsely refused, and "cosmetics" shipped no textures.

## What I did with it
- **Reliability agent (Sonnet):** launched on a new branch to fix each trigger, calibrate the plan-screen estimates from this data, and add a stats tool so the next run proves the improvement.
- **Eval:** still running with one slot at a time, so your builds never wait.
- **After the agent reports:** I verify, deploy it as image `0.12`, then re-run the failing prompts and show you the before and after.

## Already fixed today
- Refines now ship under a new version (they were being treated as "already installed").
- The coach no longer asks irrelevant caps and farming questions on a plain sword.
- cyrus.my images work (refresh your browser once).
- The live asset view and the technique flags are switched on.

The host-polish agent is also still working on the real sign-in buttons and the Servers and Wallet pages on cyrus.my. I'll bring both branches through verification and a single promote when they finish.

#!/bin/bash
# cyrus.my static landing: check, build and publish ATOMICALLY with rollback copies.   (docs/CYRUS-PLATFORM.md#site)
#
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh check                 # validate src/ (local refs exist, no hotlinks, size cap)
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh build                 # check + copy src/ to dist/ with a manifest (sha256 per file)
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh publish [--go]        # build + release + atomic swap. DRY RUN unless --go.
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh rollback [ID] [--go]  # point live at the previous (or given) release
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh list                  # releases, newest first, * = live
#   apps/cyrus-site/publish.sh import <dir>          # replace src/ with a design folder (index.html + assets/)
#
# Model (same idea as scripts/lib/seamless-release.sh): releases live in $RELEASES/<UTC>-<sha>/; the docroot nginx
# serves ($LIVE, default /var/www/cyrus.my) is a SYMLINK to one of them. Cutover = one rename(2) of a new symlink over
# the old one, so a visitor never sees a half-copied site. The first publish converts the legacy real directory into
# the symlink with `mv --exchange` (renameat2 RENAME_EXCHANGE) and keeps that directory as release "legacy-<UTC>",
# which is the rollback copy. Last $KEEP releases kept (the live one and "legacy-*" are never pruned).
# nginx needs no reload (root path unchanged; disable_symlinks is off by default).
# Env: CYRUS_SITE_FEATURED_JSON (+ _ORIGIN), CYRUS_SITE_LIVE, CYRUS_SITE_RELEASES, CYRUS_SITE_KEEP, CYRUS_SITE_HEALTH_URL (curl'd after the swap; failure =
# automatic rollback), CYRUS_SITE_HEALTH_RESOLVE (curl --resolve, to hit the origin directly). Tests point LIVE/RELEASES at a temp dir.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)"
SRC="$HERE/src"; DIST="$HERE/dist"
LIVE="${CYRUS_SITE_LIVE:-/var/www/cyrus.my}"
RELEASES="${CYRUS_SITE_RELEASES:-/var/www/cyrus.my-releases}"
KEEP="${CYRUS_SITE_KEEP:-5}"
HEALTH_URL="${CYRUS_SITE_HEALTH_URL:-}"
HEALTH_RESOLVE="${CYRUS_SITE_HEALTH_RESOLVE:-}"   # e.g. cyrus.my:443:127.0.0.1 (check the origin, not Cloudflare)
MAX_BYTES=$((40 * 1024 * 1024))

log()  { echo "==> $*"; }
die()  { echo "XX  $*" >&2; exit 1; }
GO=0; ARGS=()
for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = --go ] && GO=1 || ARGS+=("$a"); done
set -- "${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}"
run() { if [ "$GO" = 1 ]; then "$@"; else echo "    (dry run) $*"; fi; }

cmd_check() {
  [ -f "$SRC/index.html" ] || die "src/index.html missing"
  local bad=0 ref
  # Every local src/href in HTML/CSS must exist; nothing may load from another origin (the page is self-contained).

The release branch is rebuilt with the fix and re-verifying in full. The sequence after it passes, all of which I run myself:

1. Fast-forward `main` to `release/cyrus-rc4` and promote it. This ships the coach fix, the native Servers and Wallet pages, and the host links that stay on cyrus.my.
2. Publish the new landing page, so "Sign in" and "Get started" go to the real sign-in and sign-up instead of the demo.
3. Redeploy the build service as image `0.12`, which carries the refine version fix, including the designer-edit exclusion I just added.
4. Smoke-check cyrus.my pages (including `/servers` and `/wallet`), and run one refine to confirm the version and the live view.

**Note on `/servers` and `/wallet`:** the host-polish agent asked for nginx and Cloudflare allow-list changes. The fallback I added earlier already routes any path that isn't a static landing file to the app, so those pages will work without further nginx edits.

- **Eval:** running with one slot, so builds never wait.
- **Reliability agent:** still working on the first-pass failures. That will be image `0.13` after I verify it.

input.prompt:
You are building Cyrus's self-improving core on branch `feature/cyrus-recipe-memory`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-learn` (git repo of /opt/nxeon, from main ce6392c70d; work ONLY there). Read first: /root/CLAUDE.md, /root/claudeskills/agent-notes/HANDOFF-FULL.md, agent-notes/cyrus-research/{CYRUS-TRACKER.md sections 60,61,94,97, BL-recipe-memory-design.md, BL-token-savings-plan.md, BK-learning-loop.md, BJ-token-efficiency-baseline.md, BM-readiness-audit-2026-10-13.md part C+D}, docs/cyrus/15-learning-loop.md, lib/cyrus/learning/*, lib/cyrus/templates (the 24 starter templates), lib/cyrus/coach/*, lib/cyrus/planner/*, services/modbuilder/{prompts.js,route.js,server.js,autofix.js,eval/*}, scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts, scripts/cyrus/eval-journal-stats.ts, lib/cyrus/eval/*.

GOAL (owner): "a fully self-learning, self-improving, complete game mod engine", and "bring the token cost down, especially for simple mods". Measured baseline (tracker 97): 65 builds, pass@1 57.6%, repairs = 65% of spend, plain $0.15 / designer $0.37 / texture $0.50 / sound $0.49 per pass. Build, in this order (commit per task, all behind default-OFF flags registered in lib/cyrus/admin/flags.ts + settings catalog + docs):
1. STARTER BANK: prebuilt, deterministic, golden-verified mods for the house starter templates and the commonest simple archetypes (homes/warps, kits, welcome message, chat format, AFK, keep-inventory, simple custom item with stats, etc.). A request that matches a bank entry with high confidence (deterministic matcher, coach archetypes, no model) is produced with ZERO model tokens: a parameterised template compiled by the existing designer/compile path or a stored verified source tree + config, then the normal scan/Test Flight gate. The user is told honestly ("ready-made, instant, N tokens") and can still customise through the Config Studio or 'refine'. Never reproduce a user's own mod (MB_DEDUPE stays off); bank content is Nxeon-authored only. Token charge for bank hits is a settings value (default small, PLACEHOLDER).
2. RECIPE MEMORY v1 per BL-recipe-memory-design.md: verified generic mechanic recipes (what works on each Paper version: e.g. cooldown map, per-player persistent data, region-safe block loops with NxPerf, item model states, particle bursts) stored as small data files with ids, versions, compile+scan+flight proof; the guard/router returns the recipe ids relevant to the request; prompts include only those recipes (cache-friendly), A/B flag with a holdback for measurement. Seed it from the goldens in services/modbuilder/golden and the technique recipes (mc-combattag, mc-playerfx, veins, captures).
3. PATH MEMORY + candidate review: record which prompt shape -> lane/model/tier/effort path succeeded cheaply (outcome data only, anonymised per D-60/D-61, never user mod code), derive recommended defaults; the mining job (lib/cyrus/learning) outputs candidate rules/recipes/routing hints into the existing admin Learning tab review queue with accept/reject, never auto-applied.
4. EVAL GATE: `scripts/cyrus/eval-gate.ts` runs a fixed small subset (about 20 prompts, fake-able with --dry-run and a recorded-journal mode for tests), compares to services/modbuilder/eval/baseline.json and the last accepted run, writes a verdict (pass-rate, cost, regressions per lane) usable by scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh as an optional pre-promotion check and by a weekly scheduled run; wire the engine release manifest (lib/cyrus/learning/release) so each build service image has a recorded eval verdict. Do NOT run paid builds; use journals in /root/cyrus-eval/first1 (read-only) as fixtures.
5. Plan-screen honesty: show 'ready-made (instant)' vs 'built by AI' and the estimate range for each.

RULES: never build/run in /opt/nxeon; heavy commands only via `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost` from inside the worktree (`devhost tsc`, `devhost test <files>`, `devhost run -- ...`, `devhost build`, `devhost db push` throwaway DB). If a call is denied by the permission classifier, do NOT retry or work around it: note it in the report. No production actions: no deploys, no image redeploy, no env/flag/setting writes in prod, no VM writes, no paid model calls (fakes/recorded fixtures only; real flights on node-2 via devhost for compile+boot are fine). New files under services/modbuilder must be in the Dockerfile COPY list (test checks). DB: additive manual SQL only, NOT applied. Stage explicit paths, never `git add -A` at repo root. Commit with trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Docs refs: docs-build + rsync from root@178.63.94.114:/tank/nxeon-build/wt/cyrus-learn/ (and build-*-artifacts scripts for bundled validators). Warn-don't-block applies to user choices. Be economical.

FINISH: new tests for matcher precision (no false 'instant' hits on the unsafe/coverage eval sets), bank compile+scan+boot via devhost real flights (javac + Test Flight on 1.21.11 and one more version), recipe selection, candidate queue, gate verdict maths; `devhost tsc` = 0; full suite green (`devhost test test/cyrus-*.test.ts test/modbuilder-*.test.ts`; cyrus-admin flake alone); docs 02/09/11/12/15 updated. Final report under 200 words: commits, tests, flags added (all OFF), expected token impact (labelled estimate) and how it is measured, image/portal redeploy needed, unverified items.
